title: Vanishing of H_1 and of the differentials at a prime gives an etale localization
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $C$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q\subset C$ a prime ideal such that the localizations at $\mathfrak q$ of the $C$-modules $H_1(L_{C/A})$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\Omega_{C/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] vanish: $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ and $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Then there is $h\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, induced by $A\to C\to C_h$, is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-formally-etale-cotangent-criterion] at q: the hypotheses give q in Algebra.etaleLocus A C. In Lean rewrite Algebra.etaleLocus_eq_compl_support and use Module.notMem_support_iff on each of the two localized modules. Thus Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q holds.

Apply Mathlib Algebra.exists_etale_of_isEtaleAt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Locus.lean:103) to the finitely presented algebra C and the preceding IsEtaleAt instance. It gives h not in q and Algebra.Etale A (Localization.Away h). This is a single application of the existing theorem, whose proof uses openness of the etale locus and the basic-open basis; no new intermediate theory is needed.

By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the corresponding spectrum morphism is etale. In Lean apply HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff with P := @AlgebraicGeometry.Etale, then RingHom.etale_algebraMap to the ring-theoretic conclusion. Pair this with h not in q.
